Blame a shared benchmark deadline on the side that used it

Paired rounds share one measurement deadline between the candidate and
the reference, and a run that hit it was blamed on whichever side was
running. A slow candidate's overrun therefore landed on the reference
about half the time; a reference failure is retried as infrastructure
without limit and pauses the board while it waits.

In production on 2026-10-28 one slow entry kept the overall board paused
for over an hour, blocking every later entry's overall evaluation, until
an operator marked the job as the candidate's failure.

The rounds now charge each run to its side, and running out of the
shared deadline is blamed on the side that has used more of it. The
per-run cap and the reference-only calibration keep their attribution.
This changes the benchmark identity.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Compare the sides' time per run, not their totals, when a shared deadline runs out

When the shared benchmark deadline strikes, one side may have finished one run more than the
other. Comparing total time then counts that run against it: a reference at 2s a run with three
runs done (6s) outweighed a candidate at 2.4s a run with two done and a third stopped (5.5s),
and the timeout was blamed on the faster side.

Each finished run is now kept with its side, and the side with the higher mean run time is at
fault. The stopped run only bounds its own side's from below. A tie, or no evidence, still stays
with the side that was running.
